analyst_view.overall: Early view: Fiorentina are near the bottom under Vanoli despite three games unbeaten before the break, with Parisi out until at least January and Pongracic, Ranieri and Atta also injured, and De Gea's form in goal criticised. Cagliari under Pisacane play compact and on the counter, and they stopped a four-game losing run with a 1-0 win over Frosinone. Neither side plays in Europe.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean slightly higher: Fiorentina's home games have averaged 3.4 goals, with Fiorentina conceding 2.2 a game at home, and De Gea has the lowest save rate of any regular Serie A keeper. Cagliari's away games average three goals.

corners.text: The site expects 9.6 corners. I lean higher: Fiorentina's home games have averaged about 12 corners, and Cagliari concede about 6.5 corners a game. Pellegrino said Fiorentina worked all week on set pieces before scoring from one against Juventus.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean lower because Cagliari's away games have averaged under two cards, among the calmest in Serie A. Fiorentina's home games are a little higher, but not enough to reach four.

shots.text: The site expects 29.8 shots. I lean slightly higher: Fiorentina's home games have averaged almost 33 shots, with Fiorentina taking 19 a game, and Cagliari allow almost 19 shots a game. Cagliari's counter-attacking style means they shoot less.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Fiorentina's home games have averaged about 11 on target, but Cagliari's compact defence forces a lot of blocked shots, as against Frosinone's 29 attempts. I stay with the number.
